# Visual summary — connecting road + ice via the waterway (steps + zoom plots)

A visual walkthrough of the road + ice connection through the full Alaska waterway in the mmnet framework
(anchors = ports ∪ barge hubs → road & ice; plus road↔road, ice↔ice, ice↔road policies), differentiating
**connected (giant)** vs **disconnected** — now **including the waterway**. Generated by
`03_zoom_summary.py` (config: AK-only waterway, anchor max_dist 5 km, policies 3 km).

## The steps (`out/03_steps.png`)

| step | road in giant |
|---|---|
| (a) baseline — modes separate (road · ice · waterway) | 69 % |
| (b) **+ Barge transfers** (ports + barge hubs → road & ice) | 86 % |
| (c) + road↔road + ice↔ice weld + ice↔road bridge | 93 % |
| (d) **final — connected (green, incl. waterway) vs disconnected (red)** | 93 % |

The Barge transfers at ports + barge hubs do the heavy lifting; the welds/bridges tidy nearby grids and
pull ice in. Panel (d) colors **road + ice + waterway** by giant membership.

## Connected vs disconnected (`out/03_connected_vs_disconnected.png`)

Every edge — **road, ice, AND waterway** — colored **green = connected (giant)** vs **red = disconnected**,
plus the **fuel hubs as stars** colored the same way (**297 connected / 97 disconnected** of 394), with
ports (black). **Road 96 %, ice 95 %, waterway 100 %** in the giant after the **connect-to-giant** pass.
The **North Slope is now green** — joined at its ~210 m coastal barge landing; only genuinely remote pieces
(gap > 2 km) stay red.

## Zoom plots (`out/03_zooms.png`)

Five **by-sea connections** + the North Slope. The by-sea panels are the road-isolated coastal communities
that reach the network only by sea, each joined via its port/hub over the (green, connected) waterway —
e.g. **Juneau, Ketchikan, Kodiak, Craig, Haines**. The **North Slope (Barrow)** panel is **now GREEN** —
connected at its ~210 m coastal barge landing (the connect-to-giant pass).

## Takeaway

The connection follows mmnet's logic — ports + barge hubs anchor Barge↔(road ∪ ice) transfers over the
waterway, the road↔road/ice↔ice/ice↔road policies tidy up, and a final **connect-to-giant** pass joins
every leftover piece to the giant where it is within ~2 km (a coastal barge landing where road meets sea).
Green vs red makes it legible: **96 % of road, 95 % of ice, 100 % of waterway** join the giant; the North
Slope is now connected; only genuinely remote pieces stay red. Research only.
